summary: Nobuyuki Watase is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1963–1966). He served as an assistant professor at Tokai University (~1982–2007) and as president of Kobe Shukugawa Gakuin University (~2007–2010).

Nobuyuki Yoshimoto is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Otani University (~1959–1968) under Issai Funahashi and Genjun Sasaki. He held posts at Otani University (~1981–2006) and directed the Shin Buddhist Comprehensive Research Institute (~2004–2008).

Nora Kershaw Chadwick was a history and archaeology scholar who studied at Newnham College (~1911–1914). She held academic posts at the University of St Andrews (~1919–1923) and the University of Cambridge (~1950–1958).

Norbert Max Samuelson worked in philosophy and religious studies, studying at Northwestern, Hebrew Union College, and Indiana University under Shlomo Pines. His posts included Temple University (1975–1998) and Arizona State University (~1998–2018) as Grossman Professor of Jewish Studies.

Noriaki Hakamaya worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Komazawa University under Shun'ei Hirai and the University of Tokyo under Zuiho Yamaguchi, later serving as professor at Komazawa University (1985–2011) and Komazawa Junior College (1994–2006).
Noriaki Hosoda is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar. He served at Hokkaido University as an assistant (attested 1986) and later as an associate professor (attested 2003).
Noriaki Inoue is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University (~1949–1953). He later served as a professor at Taisho University (attested 1982).

Norihiko Tanaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Osaka Kyoiku University, Bukkyo University, and Visva-Bharati University. He held academic posts at Bukkyo University from 1976, serving as professor (1994, 2013) and professor emeritus (2015–2021).
Norihiko Uchida is a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied under Yutaka Ochihara. He held an assistant post at the Osaka University of Foreign Studies (attested 1962).

Norihisa Baba works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Hanazono University and the University of Tokyo under Masahiro Shimoda, later holding posts at the University of Tokyo from 2006, where he became professor in 2019.
Norio Koyama is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Shinshu University and under Seitatsu Matsunami. He served as a professor at Taisho University (attested 2014).

Noritoshi Aramaki is a Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology scholar who studied at Kyoto University. He served as professor at Osaka University (~1980–1990), Kyoto University (2000), and Otani University (~2000–2007), and director at Kyoto Koka Women's University (~2007).

Noriyuki Kudo is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Bukkyo University. He served as a lecturer at Bukkyo University (attested 1999–2000) and associate professor at Soka University (attested 2000–2022).

Norman Fischer is a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar. He studied at Colgate University, the University of Iowa, UC Berkeley, and Graduate Theological Union, trained under Sojun Mel Weitsman and Richard Baker, and founded the Everyday Zen Foundation in 2000.

Norman Mosley Penzer was a scholar of Indology attested in 1925 as a Fellow of the Royal Anthropological Institute, Royal Geographical Society, and Geological Society, and a member of the Folklore Society and Royal Asiatic Society.

Norvin Hein was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under Franklin Edgerton. He served as Associate Professor of Comparative Religion in the Divinity School at Yale University (attested 1965).

Nosei Fuji is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Dongguk University. Fuji held posts at Daegu University (1988), Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 2002–2007), and Ryukoku University as Professor of Buddhist Studies (attested 2011–2013).

Notto R. Thelle is a scholar in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He was Associate Director at the NCC Center for the Study of Japanese Religions in 1974 and held a post at the University of Oslo (~1986–2006).

Noémie Verdon works in Indology and history/archaeology. She completed her PhD at the University of Lausanne (-2015) under Johannes Bronkhorst and Charles Genequand, and later held a post at Kyoto University (attested 2018–2019).

Noël Peri was a Japanology and Buddhist studies scholar who taught Western music at Tokyo Music School (1896–1906). He later held posts as resident (1907) and secretary-librarian (1911) at the École Française d'Extrême-Orient.
